candidates.proposition: On November 12, 2026, an unexpected loss of cooling-water pressure in a shared utility loop at Micron's advanced-packaging facility forced a defined group of packaging tools into a controlled safe state, causing an unplanned interruption affecting selected high-bandwidth-memory and server-memory programs.
Micron stated that the November 12 interruption was not part of a planned maintenance event.

Other manufacturing and packaging areas at the site continued to operate during the interruption, but the incident removed available capacity from a critical advanced-packaging step used by the affected programs.
Following its initial review, Micron reduced its expected saleable-bit output for the affected packages during the current recovery period.
Micron adjusted delivery dates for a limited set of customer commitments that had been scheduled to leave the affected packaging sequence before the end of December 2026.
Micron directly informed the relevant customers of the revised delivery schedule and is working with them on revised delivery dates.

Micron stated it is not treating the output reduction as a routine sequencing adjustment because the affected output cannot be recovered by moving material through the normal weekly maintenance calendar.

Micron expects the physical repair work on the cooling-water utility equipment to conclude during the week of November 18, 2026, followed by a staged equipment return, qualification lots, and controlled restoration of normal release volumes.
Based on the current engineering plan, the affected advanced-packaging area is expected to remain in recovery through January 31, 2027.
The January 31, 2027 recovery window extends beyond the site's ordinary planned-maintenance interval, which is generally measured in hours or days rather than multiple production weeks.

Micron did not attribute the interruption to demand conditions, customer specifications, or a product-quality issue; it described the event as an operational disruption at a key manufacturing-support node.
Micron stated it will prioritize the packages associated with the revised customer commitments once qualified output becomes available, and will maintain additional process checks during the restart.
